Manufacturing Business Acquisitions in India

Manufacturing acquisitions should be evaluated through operating and financial diligence together. Capacity utilisation, plant condition, customer qualification, sustainable margins and working capital can be as important as reported revenue.

Start a private enquiry ↗

Define the industrial capability

Identify the specific process, product, capacity, certification or customer relationship you are acquiring. Evaluate whether the existing assets and operating team can support the buyer’s planned growth.

Review real manufacturing economics

Understand product mix, utilisation, yield, scrap, maintenance capital expenditure, energy costs and working-capital cycles. Reconcile production and dispatch information to financial results. Separate cyclical margin movements from sustainable operating improvements.

Identify operational diligence priorities

Review licences and environmental compliance, plant safety, maintenance records, customer approvals, supply concentration and management dependencies with appropriate technical specialists. Account for required capital expenditure when evaluating returns.

How Legacy Search can help

We originate acquisition conversations for established Indian businesses, including manufacturing, subject to mandate fit and owner willingness. Buyers should specify their process, target scale, geography and acquisition rationale in their initial brief.

Common questions

Is unused plant capacity always an upside?

No. Demand, process constraints, asset condition, staffing and capital expenditure determine whether unused capacity can be profitably activated.

Should valuation use revenue or EBITDA?

Both may inform analysis, but appropriate methods depend on earnings quality, asset intensity, growth and transaction evidence.

General information only; not legal, tax or investment advice. Transaction availability, suitability and execution depend on the circumstances.
